motion: PersistentSiteFrame maps / to the to-profile top card and keeps AnimatedTopCard mounted across route changes.

Every valid tab activation, including the current tab and rapid returns, immediately clears close timers, pointer/focus intent and active case state before early returns. Pane DOM suppression hides glass/year/stickers and restores unshifted text without transition even in retained outgoing panes. The preview portal unmounts with its AnimatePresence boundary without exit fade. Only a subsequent valid hover/focus opening in the active non-inert pane restores its hover and preview; tab re-entry alone does not. Home tabs stay on one line below the top card, with --home-top-card-to-tabs-gap (80px) from card bottom to tab-label top, --home-tabs-gap (20px) between tab labels, and --home-tabs-to-list-gap (60px) from tab-label bottom to the first list heading or first case title text in an untitled section (compensating item layout padding with a first-section negative margin), and --home-section-title-gap (40px) from section title to its first case, plus --home-section-gap (60px) from the last case subtitle to the next heading; mobile top-card/tab/list gaps follow design-system-spec.md#layout, while other listed gaps stay unchanged. Buttons use half of --space-md vertical and half of --space-xl horizontal padding on desktop and mobile; shell/label padding is compensated in layout and adjacent button bounds overlap to keep the requested label gaps; tablist left inset subtracts button padding so the first label aligns with section-heading text on desktop and mobile. The active tab has a label-width light gray --line-muted underline matching the global text-link underline color; thickness, label offset and button geometry follow design-system-spec.md#home-showcase-motion. The underline measures each label relative to the tablist, excluding button padding. Active, hover and focus-visible labels use --color-gray-700. One persistent light gray underline moves and resizes with the slower ease tween and a separate very weak scaleX spring defined canonically in design-system-spec.md#home-showcase-motion. Rapid clicks retarget from current position, width and unfinished scale without a reset jump; repeated activation can replay the weak spring. Initial placement, resize and reduced motion reset the scale; reduced motion is instant and unmount stops all underline animations. On mobile, horizontal touch swipes across the full-width region below tabs select adjacent tabs without wrapping: left next, right previous. The hit area includes the tab-to-list gap, list rows and blank space down to the viewport bottom, using a measured minimum height without shifting content. Direction lock, gesture threshold and synthetic-click suppression follow design-system-spec.md#home-showcase-motion. Native vertical scroll, ordinary link taps and keyboard activation remain; controls, editable content and nested scrollable widgets are excluded. Swipe uses the shared tab activation path and does not cover the top card or tabs. Active tab title persists in sessionStorage without changing the URL and restores by remounting the pane-presence boundary before paint, without a switch transition or overlapping panes. Incoming and outgoing targets travel 80px in opposite directions with 20ms incoming stagger and a 1129ms complete switch: incoming movement/visibility duration is 929ms minus (N-1)*20ms for N actually animated targets, with elapsed preparation time deducted and stagger capped to the remaining budget; outgoing movement, opacity and 10px blur use 200ms without stagger. The first incoming target starts 200ms after the first outgoing target starts, so the waves overlap. The incoming pane enters normal flow immediately while the outgoing pane remains mounted out of flow until its final row completes. The viewport does not clip content. Reduced motion is instant.

Home tablist uses page-level reveal. Each keyed tab pane owns a nested wave reveal for section headings and case items; initial entry and sessionStorage restoration wait for scroll restoration and use zero horizontal offset, while click switches prepare the new wave after two animation frames and delay its first target until 200ms after the outgoing wave starts. Rapid re-entry restarts that pane's wave. Each incoming target combines signed 80px horizontal movement and no vertical travel, staggered 20ms per target. The full switch ends at 1129ms from outgoing start; after the 200ms offset, movement/visibility duration is 929ms minus (N-1)*20ms for N actually animated targets. Late preparation subtracts elapsed time and exceptionally long waves cap the stagger to the remaining budget. Outgoing targets move in the mirror direction over 200ms without stagger, starting from their current computed transform if interrupted. Neither pane has whole-panel horizontal travel; each case glass and preview still waits for its own target readiness. Initial page entry retains the shared 80ms row stagger; initialized nested reveal targets are isolated. In scripting-enabled browsers, server-rendered CSS hides uninitialized leaf targets in pending roots before hydration, including the complete tablist and active underline; no-JS and reduced-motion content stays visible.

Case-item glass and preview are gated by per-target reveal readiness: only opacity/filter visibility animations of that target must settle; movement may continue, including its own stagger. Hover or focus held on the item opens automatically when it becomes ready; instant and reduced-motion targets are ready immediately. This does not wait for the global reveal sequence or block link navigation.

Active case glass position uses velocity-preserving physics with mass 0.9: smoothstep remains for stiffness 320..460, while a reference damping curve of approximately 0.80..0.62 uses a normalized exponential ease-out measured in actual item steps with scale 4.5. The start-from-rest theoretical peak stays physical and unchanged through 12px, then an exponential target-amplitude curve toward an 18px asymptote is converted into effective damping (approximately 0.7566 at maximum travel). Approach crossing time is normalized to 1.20x the reference spring with damping-aware flight compensation; the post-target distance-aware tail time-warp remains 1x..2x. Initial inherited velocity is pre-compensated for the active flight scale in copied spring options; size morph uses 220/22/1.0.

Pointer shift targets ±16px/±10px through a 300/24/0.75 spring with power 1.4; active text follows 25% over 420ms expressive easing. Year bracket and label move together without rotation from independent group-coordinate pointer targets, with amplitude and the 300/24/0.75 springs defined by the year-group contract; reveal-ready hover/focus has no extra delay and fades/deblurs over 1120ms, then exits immediately over 280ms. Outgoing text returns over 600ms standard easing; glass perspective and the 380ms close delay remain unchanged.
Hover preview is a fine-pointer desktop enhancement and swaps media with blur/opacity/scale transitions; reduced motion uses opacity only.

Incoming movement, opacity and blur use 929ms minus (N-1)*20ms for N actually animated targets, so the full switch ends 1129ms after outgoing start. Late preparation subtracts elapsed time and exceptionally long waves cap the stagger. Outgoing movement, opacity and blur(10px) retain 200ms without stagger. Interrupted outgoing targets start from their computed transform. The first incoming target begins 200ms after the first outgoing target, overlapping the two staggered waves. There is no whole-panel horizontal travel. One persistent light gray --line-muted label-width underline matches the global text-link underline color and moves/resizes with the slower ease tween plus a separate very weak scaleX spring defined canonically in design-system-spec.md#home-showcase-motion. Rapid clicks retarget current position, width and unfinished scale without a reset jump; repeated activation can replay the weak spring. Initial placement, resize and reduced motion reset scale; reduced motion is instant and unmount stops all underline animations. Tab title persists in sessionStorage and restores by remounting pane presence before paint, without entrance animation or overlapping panes. The incoming pane determines page height immediately; the outgoing pane remains mounted out of flow through its final row's exit. The viewport does not clip content. Keyed list and item refs survive during exit; exiting panes ignore pointer and focus events and cannot close active glass. Each case item's glass and preview wait for that item's own opacity/filter visibility animations to settle, then auto-open while movement may continue for a stationary pointer or retained focus; instant and reduced-motion items are ready immediately.
Active case text follows 25% of pointer shift over 420ms expressive easing; outgoing text returns through WAAPI over 600ms standard easing, and re-entry preserves its current visual transform.

Glass position preserves spring velocity: smoothstep maps distance to stiffness 320..460, and a separate 4.5-step exponential reference damping curve runs from approximately 0.80 to 0.62. Its theoretical start-from-rest overshoot is unchanged through 12px, then an exponential amplitude target toward 18px is converted into effective spring damping, reaching approximately 0.7566 at maximum travel. There is no visual post-crossing compression: the spring peaks and reverses physically. Damping-aware flight scaling normalizes approach crossing to 1.20x the reference spring, then the existing distance-aware 1x..2x tail scale takes over; copied spring options pre-compensate inherited velocity for the active flight scale; size uses a 220/22/1.0 lightweight morph spring.
Glass follows pointer targets ±16px/±10px with restrained transform depth and 1400px perspective.

Each pane renders one bracket per work year group, independent of itemStickers. motion: MDX headings, paragraphs, list items, blockquotes, sections, and media wrappers reveal sequentially.

Lightbox scroll locking compensates the actual body width expansion, including stable gutter space on pages without vertical overflow, according to design-system-spec.md#gallery-fullscreen-overlay-gallerylightbox. The shared rule applies to full cases, short cases and About; closing restores the original inline styles.

Lightbox arrows, thumbnails and context card wait 120ms after opening geometry completes, then fade from opacity 0 to 1 over 400ms. Pointer/focus cannot bypass this once-per-session gate; reduced motion skips the fade and media navigation does not restart the delay.

After the opening gate, desktop arrow and thumbnail hit areas remain active when their visuals fade. A stationary pointer keeps the close indicator suppressed; clicking an invisible arrow navigates and clicking an invisible thumbnail selects its media. Suppression clears only on actual pointer exit or lightbox close.
The lower white lightbox gradient declaration is retained as a CSS comment and does not render. Progressive blur extends 60px above the base lower-control region.

Static 0/8/16px ProgressiveBlur filter layers retain the existing mask positions and fade with the controls over 400ms through animated mask alpha, without animating filter opacity or wrapper opacity; reduced motion makes the fade immediate.

GalleryLightboxScope combines openable image and video items across full-case Gallery blocks. GalleryLightbox keeps a persistent shell and decoded low-resolution DOM image layers; only current/adjacent full-resolution layers are retained. Selection, context and final geometry change immediately, with no crossfade or re-open animation; context glass, title and body transitions are disabled during media navigation, and remounted context wrappers do not replay initial opacity fade. A cold target leaves an empty image area, without loading labels, placeholders or error messages. Rail centering and active crop expansion share a fixed 200ms duration. On desktop, clicks in the free horizontal track outside the occupied thumbnail region close the lightbox; the occupied thumbnails and their internal gaps remain interactive. The top-layer floating close indicator hides over a semantic flex wrapper containing only real thumbnails and their internal gaps, while outer centering spacers stay outside the hover zone; both full-height navigation zones and the context card suppress it through a Set of active region IDs without pointermove geometry reads. Only the collapsed 92%-white context card with a 12px backdrop blur is hug-sized, with a regular black title, 8px/20.8px token padding and pill radius. Actionable cards spring-expand to 560px on hover/focus with a local 420/36/1.6 spring for width, vertical padding and details height, retaining --space-xl horizontal padding and changing the radius linearly over 400ms from half the measured compact height to the bubble radius in both directions, crossfade the title to heavy over 60ms and reveal body copy (up to three lines) from below the clipped card edge: body text moves only vertically from 80px below its expanded position after 120ms with the title vertical-axis 420/36/1.6 spring and opacity fades from 0 to 1 over 200ms after 160ms; reverse has no delay. A fixed centering wrapper keeps the card centered and its bottom edge fixed. The glass surface contains a native desktop link or a semantic mobile toggle button; invisible geometry drives its height, while an independently centered fixed-width content layer avoids text scaling, reflow and expanded-title ellipsis during the width spring. Compact width hugs the complete regular title until the viewport cap with 16px per side, then applies single-line ellipsis; sizer, explicit-width anchor and glass share that cap, with the 10px hover inset outside the surface, and both title weights are anchored to the fixed-width inner content layer and travel independently of glass resize from compact center to expanded upper-left while crossfading; both title positions follow the same oval arc: both directions use the glass spring stiffness and damping with 90% of its mass (default 420/36/1.44), retaining spring overshoot at both endpoints. The compact hover zone is 20px wider than the compact card in total (10px each side); the expanded card holds hover inside that zone until pointer exit, without a re-entry lock. Optional ?lightboxDebug=1 exposes a nonpersistent panel for shared resize/title/text spring stiffness, damping and mass, text travel distance, text-rise delay, opacity delay/duration, title crossfade duration, radius duration and Reset, only while an actionable context card is open. Defaults: glass/body spring 420/36/1.6 and title spring 420/36/1.44, text travel 80px, rise delay 120ms, fade delay 160ms, fade duration 200ms, title crossfade 60ms, radius duration 400ms. On mobile, card tap or Enter/Space toggles expansion and repeated activation collapses it. Desktop hover/focus expands the card, surface activation navigates after closing, and the pointer informer reads Показать в кейсе. Only mobile expanded cards show a separate Показать в кейсе CTA with --color-accent-blue background, --color-white text, --radius-pill and desktop informer padding --space-xs / --space-lg-compact, separated by --space-sm and filling the text content width with centered text; invisible expanded geometry includes its height. The mobile CTA stays mounted, follows body travel/spring/fade with the canonical 80ms sibling stagger added to opening delays, reverses without delay and is disabled/unfocusable/pointer-inactive when collapsed. Mobile compact title measurements use intrinsic layer sizes instead of animated glass bounds; collapse does not remeasure or force instant motion. On mobile, toggle and CTA are sibling buttons; only the CTA navigates after closing and releasing the scroll lock. The transformed content layer stacks above the surface toggle and ignores pointer events except for its CTA, keeping the CTA hit target unobstructed. On touch, the first card tap expands and the second collapses; with expanded context, a tap outside the text preview collapses only the preview with its reverse animation, including central media taps. With collapsed context, tapping outside the current media container closes the lightbox. Explicit navigation through media side zones, swipe, arrows or thumbnails preserves expansion; actual controls and the CTA execute their own actions without outside capture. Mobile navigation preserves the expanded context and replaces its content instantly; mobile focus changes do not collapse the card before CTA activation. The left/right 20% of the actual media container navigate non-cyclically; the central 60% retains image double-tap zoom (the whole media area for one item). Pinch zoom 1x-4x and double-tap 1x/2x enlarge and reposition the media shell itself around the gesture origin, without inner-asset clipping; zoom resets on media change/close and disables one-finger swipe above 1x. With collapsed text preview, outside the current media shell taps close the lightbox; with expanded preview, ordinary outside taps collapse only the preview, excluding legitimate controls; synthetic clicks following pinch/swipe are suppressed. Desktop interaction is preserved. Full cases use the nearest preceding heading (or the case title before the first heading) and the first nonempty paragraph of that section for every media, regardless of caption. Media in the same Gallery share the same title and paragraph. The full card surface navigates on desktop and toggles expansion on mobile; mobile source navigation is available through the separate CTA only. Short cases show only the caption heading in a compact non-expanding card and hide it without a caption. About has no context card. Keyboard-open sessions restore focus on ordinary close, but ArrowLeft navigation to the previous item and ArrowRight navigation to the next item suppress restoration to the source media because the active item changed; keyboard navigation does not reveal hidden controls, and subsequent Tab navigation may enable accessible restoration again. Non-cyclic navigation, responsive controls, source-aware close motion and reduced-motion fallback remain; the short-case render gets an isolated scope.

The portfoliocase MDX can render a non-interactive three-scene PortfolioMotionDemo in a fixed-height white borderless viewport: top card, short mode, and one Portfolio as a Product case. The motion rhythm is slowed by 1.2x: outgoing travels from 0 to 120px over 720ms with cubic-bezier(0.7, 0, 0.84, 0), while incoming reaches the apex at the 1440ms lifecycle boundary with mirrored cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1). Outgoing opacity stays at 1 and blur at 0px through the first 60px, then changes to 0 and 18px. Incoming starts when outgoing opacity reaches 0.5 at about 683ms and is fully opaque and deblurred after its first 60px at about 760ms. Equal scene visibility peaks at about 24.4/24.4 percent, below the 30/30 limit. Every scene crosses 0deg into the opposite rotation, following either -15deg -> 0deg -> 15deg or 15deg -> 0deg -> -15deg, with starting directions alternating continuously across the loop. The opacity >= 0.8 guard starts the production animations: the top-card to-profile -> to-home switch and the short-mode switch each wait 280ms before starting, all top-card states continuously run the production 620ms icon hover cycle, and short mode remains 2x. Top card keeps --home-top-card-width on every viewport; the single case keeps the production bubble's natural text-sized proportions, is uniformly scaled to 1.2x, and is centered in the scene, proportionally enlarging its text, sticker, radius, shadows, and bubble deformation. The case combines entry and exit into one continuous trajectory without pausing at the apex, and changes opacity and blur only after its first 60px on either leg. Its glass bubble waits 140ms after the case appears, fades over 280ms, and scales from 0.1 to 1 with a spring tail using 220 / 14 / 1 before the sticker frame cycle begins. The viewport is 412px high and shifts the scene center upward by 68.8px, placing the trajectory apex at about 137.2px versus the upper-third target of about 137.3px. The remaining lower area contains the full fall, rotation, blur tail, and case scale without clipping. Every exiting scene calls safeToRemove after 720ms, so a cyclic key cannot reuse an instance with already-mutated motion values. A visibility-aware timeout pauses while the document is hidden and resets one presence session on return, preventing accumulated exit layers. The explicit loop handoff and reduced-motion fallback remain non-interactive.
